chunks: And in the narration of al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
"Fasting is for the sighting, and breaking the fast is for the sighting, and sighting is not that one person sees it, nor two, nor fifty."

key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةِ: the sighting of the moon as the basis for legal determination
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm (fasting), specifically the commencement of the fast
key_terms.الْفِطْرُ: breaking the fast, meaning ending the fasting period at the month’s completion
key_terms.خَمْسُونَ: fifty individuals, mentioned as insufficient in the stated context

ai.seo_question: How is the start and end of Ramadan established according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the beginning and ending of the fasting month are tied to the sighting of the moon. It also indicates that sighting is not established merely by the claim of one, two, or even fifty individuals in the sense intended here.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1910 - In the narration of al-Qasim ibn Uruwah from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdullah (as), he said:
"Fasting is based on sighting [the crescent], and breaking the fast is based on sighting [the crescent]. Sighting is not determined by one person, nor two, nor fifty."
